summary: Jayandra Soni is an indologist, philosopher, and religious studies scholar. He completed Ph.D. studies at Banaras Hindu University (~1975–1978) and McMaster University (~1978–1987), and served as a Lecturer in Indology and Tibetology at the University of Marburg (~1991–2012).
Jaś Elsner works in the fields of history, archaeology, and religious studies. He has held academic posts at the University of Michigan and the University of Chicago (~2013).
Jean Dantinne worked in Buddhist studies. He studied under Étienne Lamotte and held a position as a librarian at the University of Liège.

Jean Filliozat (1906–1982) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at INALCO (~1928–1932). He served as a professor at the Collège de France (1951–1978) and directed the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1956–1977).

Jean Philippe Vogel (1871–1958) studied at the University of Amsterdam (~1890–1897), specializing in Indology and archaeology. He served with the Archaeological Survey of India (1910–1911) and was a director at Leiden University (attested 1910; 1914–1939).

Jean Przyluski (1885–1944) studied at EPHE in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He taught at INALCO (1923) and held chairs at EPHE (~1926–1930) and the Collège de France (~1931–1944), also founding Bibliographie bouddhique.

Jean-Baptiste Biot (1774–1862) studied at Collège Louis-le-Grand, École polytechnique (1794–1797), and École des Ponts et Chaussées (1794). Active in history, archaeology, and sinology, he held posts at the Collège de France (1800–1862) and Science Faculty of Paris (1809–1862).

Jean-François Jarrige (1940–2014) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the Lycée Claude Fauriel and the École du Louvre, and later served as the head of the Musée Guimet (~1986–2008).

Jean-Louis Burnouf (1775–1844), working in linguistics, studied at Collège d'Harcourt and under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy (~1815). He held posts at Lycée Louis-le-Grand (~1808–1817), ENS (~1811–1822), the University of Paris (~1817–1844), and Collège de France (1817–1844).
Jean-Luc Achard specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He was educated at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and holds a post at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique.

Jean-Luc Chevillard works in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure in 1975 and held a research post at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique starting around 1991.

Jean-Noël Robert works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at ENLOV, INALCO, and under Bernard Frank (~1970–1978). He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1990–2011) and the Collège de France (2011–2022).
Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat (1788–1832) was a Sinologist and linguist who studied at INALCO. He served as Professor of Chinese at the Collège de France from 1815 to 1832.

Jeannine Auboyer (1912–1990) specialized in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Académie Julian, École du Louvre (1929–1934), and EPHE (~1931–1942), later holding posts at CNRS (~1942–1952) and the Musée Guimet (1965–1980).
Jeff Dolven studied at Worcester College (~1989–1991) and Yale University (~1992–1998). He founded Princeton University and held a post there around 2001.
Jeff Malpas is a philosopher who served as a professor at the University of Tasmania beginning around 1999 and held a post at La Trobe University in 2019.
Jeff Wilson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill and studied under mentors Taitetsu Unno and Myōsei Tatsuguchi.

Jeffery D. Long is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago (~1993–2000) and became Associate Professor of Religion and Asian Studies at Elizabethtown College around 2000.

Jeffrey Clark Ruff studied at Missouri State University and UCSB (PhD 2002) under David Gordon White, Barbara A. Holdrege, and William F. Powell. In religious studies and Indology, he held posts at UNC, Missouri State, UC, and Marshall University (2002).

Jeffrey Davis Schoening specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under advisor Sanghasen Singh and completed his Ph.D. in 1991 at the University of Washington under doctoral supervisor Collett Cox.
